title: M166 · Wednesday prep: the Scout half-C runner and a navgrid tool tested on a synthetic grid
summary: Your Wednesday session is now 22 one-line steps that only produce data, in a phone sheet with a copy button on each command. Part A (Scout, on a local branch that the overseer fast-forwards into M156 after PASS) adds python -m scout.halfc, which writes the whole first draft of half C from a run dir: the facts table, the scored tracks, wards and recalls next to your hand check, the plots, and docs/scout-findings.md with a computed go/no-go per signal and a route. It also adds a session driver, so nothing is typed again after the sign-out; match.json saved without player identifiers; and session send, which copies the run to brain by scp and never to GitHub. There are 80 tests (34 earlier plus 46 new). The weights could not be checked on brain (2 GB of memory free, the floor is 3 GB), so skip step 9 and use the Google Drive download. Part B (this branch) adds tools/navgrid: a WAD reader, the v7.1 grid parser with both flag readings, pc-run with validation, and a GeoJSON vectoriser. It has 60 tests, all on synthetic files, and is licensed AGPL-3.0-only because the converter it ports from grants no 'or later'. Nothing derived from a real Riot file is committed. R2 checks the real grid on brain after Wednesday. Report: REPORT-R1.md.

questions.text: (react) Go/no-go thresholds for half C (proposed in tools/scout/scout/thresholds.json). Minimap positions (A): GO at median error ≤350 world units (about one brush width), detection ≥0.85 and longest gap ≤15 s (deaths excluded); PARTIAL (dashed, coarse) at median ≤700 and detection ≥0.60. Top-down (B): GO at median ≤150 and health-bar hit rate ≥0.80. Wards, per team: precision ≥0.80, recall ≥0.70, hand check ≥4 of 5. Recalls: precision ≥0.80 against purchase bursts, recall ≥0.70, hand check ≥4 of 5. Route: A and B GO gives A+B; B only gives B-first; A only, or B not reached, gives A-only; neither gives no-go. Half C may override the route only with a written reason.

chips.label: Keep as proposed
chips.consequence: Half C scores your run against these numbers as they are.

chips.label: Edit (free text)
chips.consequence: Write the numbers you want; they go into thresholds.json before half C runs.

questions.recommend: Keep as proposed. Each number maps to something the board can show: one brush width for A, a lane-side read for B.
